definition: Lernmatrix (German for "learning matrix") is a special type of artificial neural network (ANN) architecture, similar to associative memory, invented around 1960 by Karl Steinbuch, a pioneer in computer science and ANNs.
details: This model for learning systems could establish complex associations between certain sets of characteristics (e.g., letters of an alphabet) and their meanings.

explainer.lead: Lernmatrix (German for 'learning matrix') is a type of artificial neural network architecture similar to associative memory, invented around 1960 by Karl Steinbuch. It is an early model of learning systems, predating much of modern neural network work.

tiers.eli5: It's a 1960s 'learning grid' that could link a pattern, like a letter, to what it means — a very early ancestor of today's neural networks.
tiers.practitioner: It is studied as an associative-memory-style architecture that learns associations between sets of characteristics and their meanings; a pitfall is assuming it has the capacity of modern networks, since it is a historical model.
tiers.paperLevel: A special type of artificial neural network architecture, similar to associative memory; it could establish complex associations between certain sets of characteristics (e.g., letters of an alphabet) and their meanings.

explainer.example: A Lernmatrix can be trained to associate the set of characteristics making up a letter with its meaning, forming a simple associative memory.
